decks.module: Who must hold a license and residency deadlines

cards.front: What age and credential do you need to drive any motor vehicle, motor-driven cycle or moped on Colorado public roads?
cards.back: Anyone driving a motor vehicle, motor-driven cycle or moped on public roads in Colorado has to be at least sixteen years old and carry a valid driver license.

cards.front: What are some examples that make you a Colorado resident?
cards.back: Colorado counts you as a resident if, for example, you own or run a business in the state, have lived there continuously for ninety days, or hold a job there.

cards.front: After you become a Colorado resident, how long do you have to get a Colorado driver license?
cards.back: Once you become a Colorado resident, you have thirty days to get a Colorado driver license.

cards.front: Who is not held to the deadline for getting a Colorado license after moving?
cards.back: The thirty-day licensing deadline does not apply to active-duty U.S. military members, their dependents, or people living in Colorado mainly to further their education.

cards.front: How quickly must you tell the DMV about a new name or address?
cards.back: If your name or address changes, you must tell the Division of Motor Vehicles within thirty days.

cards.front: Which Colorado deadlines are thirty days, and which residency example is ninety days?
cards.back: Three different Colorado deadlines share the same length: getting a Colorado license after becoming a resident and reporting a name or address change are both thirty days, while the residency example is ninety days of continuous living in the state.

decks.module: Written test and the instruction permit

cards.front: What does the written knowledge test cover, and where can you practice?
cards.back: The written knowledge test draws on the whole handbook, including road signs, driving under the influence, driving rules, safety rules and legal topics; practice quizzes are offered online and in the myColorado app.

cards.front: When do offices stop giving written tests each day?
cards.back: Offices stop giving written tests thirty minutes before their scheduled closing time, so arrive earlier than that.

cards.front: How is the written test closing cutoff different from the thirty-day deadlines?
cards.back: The written test is not offered in the final thirty minutes before closing, which is a scheduling rule and is different from the thirty-day residency and address-change deadlines.

cards.front: What does passing the written test make you eligible for?
cards.back: Passing a written test makes you eligible for an instruction permit, which gives a learner limited driving privileges.

cards.front: Who must ride with you while you drive on an instruction permit, and where do they sit?
cards.back: While driving on an instruction permit, you need a supervising driver aged twenty-one or older, holding a valid Colorado license, in the front passenger seat.

cards.front: How do the minimum driving age and the permit supervisor age differ?
cards.back: The general minimum age to drive in Colorado is sixteen, but a permit supervisor must be at least twenty-one; do not mix up the driver age with the supervisor age.

cards.front: Who gives most drive tests in Colorado?
cards.back: State driver license offices do not currently schedule drive tests; some county-run offices do, and most drive tests are given by certified commercial driving schools.

cards.front: What does the examiner check on your vehicle before a drive test?
cards.back: Before a drive test the examiner checks the vehicle for safety, including brake lights, turn signals, seat belts, windshield and tires, and confirms the doors and windows open from inside; a vehicle you supply needs current insurance and registration.

cards.front: Who may be in the car during a drive test, and what must you put away?
cards.back: During the drive test only you and the examiner may be in the car: no interpreters, family, friends or pets; remove any weapons, switch off the radio, phone and other electronics, and clear the dashboard and rearview mirror.

cards.front: If you fail the drive test, when can you try again?
cards.back: If you fail the drive test, you cannot retake it until the next business day.

cards.front: Does the next-business-day retake wait apply to the written test?
cards.back: A failed drive test can be retaken on the next business day; that wait applies to the drive test, not to the written knowledge test.

cards.front: Will the examiner ever ask you to break the law, and when should you ask questions?
cards.back: The examiner will never ask you to break the law; ask your questions before the test starts, because you are scored the entire time and extra talking only interferes.

cards.front: Which three skill categories does the drive test assess?
cards.back: The drive test follows AAMVA guidelines and assesses three skill categories: perceptual (seeing gaps and hazards), motor (operating the controls) and attentional (focusing and shifting attention).

cards.front: Which maneuvers make up your drive test score?
cards.back: Your drive test score comes from six maneuvers: left and right turns, stopping at intersections, driving through intersections, changing lanes in traffic, general driving behavior, and merging into and leaving traffic.

cards.front: What does lane selection mean on the drive test?
cards.back: Lane selection is graded: enter and leave traffic from the correct lane, approach intersections in the correct lane, and finish each maneuver in the correct lane.
cards.memory_hook: right lane in, right lane out

cards.front: What does lane management require during turns?
cards.back: Lane management is graded: stay entirely within the turning lane, keep both hands on the wheel, and steer with an approved method such as hand-over-hand or push-pull-slide.

cards.front: Where in your lane do you begin a right turn and a left turn?
cards.back: When turning right, start from the right-most part of your lane; when turning left, start from the left-most part of your lane.

cards.front: Where should your car end up after a turn?
cards.back: After a turn, settle the car in the center of the proper lane and never cross lane markings or ride over curbs.

cards.front: What mistake do candidates often make about where a turn begins?
cards.back: For a right turn you begin from the right-most part of your lane and for a left turn from the left-most part; candidates often reverse these or start from the lane center.
cards.memory_hook: right from right, left from left

cards.front: How far ahead must your turn signal stay on in town and on four-lane highways?
cards.back: Keep your turn signal on continuously for one hundred feet before turning or changing lanes in urban areas, and for two hundred feet before doing so on four-lane highways.

cards.front: How soon must you cancel your turn signal after the move?
cards.back: Cancel your turn signal within three seconds after you finish the turn or lane change.

cards.front: How does the signal distance change with the road, and what is the cancel rule?
cards.back: The turn signal distance depends on the road: one hundred feet in urban areas versus two hundred feet on four-lane highways, and either way the signal is canceled within three seconds after the move.

cards.front: What does good speed control look like on the drive test?
cards.back: Good speed control means slowing smoothly without holding up traffic, keeping a steady speed through a lane change, and reaching an intersection slowly enough to turn without braking mid-turn.

cards.front: What makes a stop correct on the drive test?
cards.back: A correct stop has no forward motion, stays behind the stop line and crosswalk, and keeps the front wheels pointed straight until you begin the turn.

cards.front: When stopped behind another vehicle, how do you know you are far enough back?
cards.back: When stopped behind another vehicle, you are far enough back if you can see where its rear tires touch the pavement.

cards.front: What should you avoid when accelerating?
cards.back: Accelerate smoothly: do not jerk, lug the engine, coast, clash gears, stall, or hold up traffic.

cards.front: What searching habits are expected while driving?
cards.back: Searching means scanning traffic, checking over your shoulder before a lane change, using mirrors, looking left, right, then left again before entering an intersection, and looking behind after every turn.

cards.front: Can driver-assist cameras and warnings replace your own searching?
cards.back: Back-up cameras and blind-spot or lane-departure warnings may be used during the drive test, but they never replace your own physical searching.

cards.front: What form must applicants under eighteen include, and who may sign it?
cards.back: Applicants under eighteen must include an Affidavit of Liability (form DR2460), signed by a parent, stepparent, grandparent with power of attorney, legal guardian, spouse over eighteen, or another responsible adult who accepts legal liability.

cards.front: Who witnesses the affidavit signing, and what happens if the signer withdraws?
cards.back: The affidavit is signed before a driver license office employee or a notary; the signer becomes legally responsible for your driving and may withdraw, which cancels your permit or license; minors in foster care can be exempt under certain conditions.

cards.front: When can a spouse sign the Affidavit of Liability, and what does withdrawal do?
cards.back: The Affidavit of Liability signer can be a spouse only if that spouse is older than eighteen, and withdrawing the signature cancels the minor permit or license.

cards.front: How long must a minor hold an instruction permit before applying for a license?
cards.back: A minor must hold an instruction permit for twelve months before applying for a driver license.

cards.front: What driving log must a minor applicant turn in?
cards.back: A minor applicant must turn in a signed driving log showing fifty hours of driving, including ten hours at night.

cards.front: Are the night hours in the minor driving log added on top of the total?
cards.back: The minor log requires fifty total hours, of which ten must be at night; the night hours are part of the total, not added on top.

cards.front: Which minor applicants must also take behind-the-wheel training, and how much?
cards.back: Applicants younger than sixteen and six months must also complete six hours of behind-the-wheel training with an approved driver education instructor.

cards.front: When can extra supervised hours replace the instructor training hours?
cards.back: If no approved school within thirty miles of home offers at least twenty hours of behind-the-wheel training per week, twelve extra hours with a parent, guardian or alternate permit supervisor may replace the six instructor hours; bring a printed route map if the nearest commercial school is more than thirty miles away.

cards.front: Who must take the instructor hours, and when is the substitute allowed?
cards.back: The six hours of behind-the-wheel instruction apply only to applicants younger than sixteen and six months, and the twelve extra supervised hours are a substitute only where no qualifying school is within thirty miles.

decks.module: Passenger and curfew limits for new minors

cards.front: What passenger limit applies in a minor's first six months of licensure?
cards.back: For the first six months after a driver under eighteen is licensed, no passengers under twenty-one are allowed unless a parent or another licensed adult driver is in the car.

cards.front: How do passenger limits change after six months and after one year?
cards.back: From six months to one year of licensure, a driver under eighteen may carry one passenger under twenty-one, with siblings and passengers in a medical emergency as exceptions; after one year, passengers may equal the number of seat belts.

cards.front: How do passenger limits step up during a minor's first year?
cards.back: Passenger limits step up with time licensed: none under twenty-one in the first six months without an adult driver, one under twenty-one after six months, and as many as there are seat belts after one year.

cards.front: During the first year, when may a minor not drive, and what are the exceptions?
cards.back: During the first year of licensure, a minor may not drive between midnight and five a.m. unless accompanied by an instructor, parent or legal guardian; exceptions cover trips to school or work with a signed statement, medical emergencies and emancipated minors.

cards.front: What hours does the first-year curfew cover, and what excuses a school or work trip?
cards.back: The curfew window for first-year minors runs from midnight to five a.m., and a school or work trip is excused only with a signed statement from the school or employer.
cards.memory_hook: signed note for school or work

decks.module: Ways to lose your driving privilege

cards.front: What can get your driving privilege suspended, revoked or canceled?
cards.back: Your driving privilege can be suspended, revoked or canceled if you reach the point total for suspension, are convicted of driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs, or refuse an alcohol or drug test.

cards.front: What crash-related conduct can cost you your license?
cards.back: Leaving a crash scene without stopping, exchanging information and giving aid, or failing to report a crash to the DMV under the Financial Responsibility Law, can also cost you your license.

cards.front: What other grounds can cost you your license?
cards.back: Other grounds for losing your license include lying on your application, not settling a crash judgment, lending or misusing your license, skipping a DMV re-examination, and a vehicular homicide conviction.

cards.front: Can conduct after a crash cost you your license, apart from points or impaired driving?
cards.back: Losing your license can come from conduct after a crash, such as leaving the scene or not reporting it under the Financial Responsibility Law, not only from driving under the influence or points.

recaps.module: Who must hold a license and residency deadlines

recap_hooks.text: You must be at least sixteen with a valid license, and new residents get a Colorado license within thirty days.
Name and address changes go to the DMV within thirty days; the residency example is ninety days of living here.

recaps.module: Written test and the instruction permit

recap_hooks.text: Passing the written test earns a permit, and the supervisor must be twenty-one or older in the front seat.
Arrive well before closing, because written tests stop thirty minutes early.
Only you and the examiner ride along, the car must be safe, insured and registered, and a failed drive test waits until the next business day.
Start a right turn from the right side of your lane and a left turn from the left side, then finish centered.
Signal one hundred feet ahead in town, two hundred on four-lane highways, and cancel within three seconds.
Stop fully behind the line and far enough back to see the rear tires ahead.
Search with your own eyes; cameras and warnings only help.
Minors need a signed affidavit, twelve months on a permit, and a fifty-hour log with ten hours at night.
Younger applicants also need six hours with an instructor unless no school is nearby.

recaps.module: Passenger and curfew limits for new minors

recap_hooks.text: No young passengers for six months, one for the next six, then as many as there are seat belts.
First-year minors stay off the road from midnight to five unless an exception applies.

recaps.module: Ways to lose your driving privilege

recap_hooks.text: Points, impaired driving, test refusal and leaving a crash scene can all cost you your license.
